sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰。

sentences.en: And I'm Mark Ronson.
sentences.zh: 我是马克·朗森。

sentences.en: And welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《重构者》，这是一档专注于设计之美及其周边文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl, every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you, and you turned a DJ booth
sentences.zh: 即便是在黑胶唱片时代的夜店做DJ时，你每晚也要带着300件你最珍视的宝贝去工作，然后你把DJ台

sentences.en: into this, like, living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 变成了一个活生生的、充满50年历史精美文物的快闪博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听爱彼带来的《重构者》吧。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴尔巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Today, a Republican senator publishes a book criticizing the president and saying, quote, we have given in to the politics of anger.
sentences.zh: 今天，一位共和党参议员出版了一本书，批评总统并称，引用原文，“我们已经屈服于愤怒的政治”。

sentences.en: Now the president is going after him in his home state of Arizona and mocking him for being weak on immigration.
sentences.zh: 现在总统正在他的家乡亚利桑那州对他发起攻击，嘲笑他在移民问题上软弱无能。

sentences.en: The feud between Jeff Flake and Donald Trump and what it reveals about the mounting tensions between the president and Congress.
sentences.zh: 杰夫·弗莱克与唐纳德·特朗普之间的不和，揭示了总统与国会之间日益紧张的关系。

sentences.en: It's Friday, August 25th.
sentences.zh: 今天是8月25日，星期五。

sentences.en: And nobody wants me to talk about your other senator who's weak on borders, weak on crime, so I won't talk about him.
sentences.zh: 没人想让我谈论你们那位在边境问题上软弱、在犯罪问题上软弱的另一位参议员，所以我不会谈论他。

sentences.en: Nobody wants me to talk about him.
sentences.zh: 没人想让我谈论他。

sentences.en: Nobody knows who the hell he is.
sentences.zh: 没人知道他到底是谁。

sentences.en: And now, see, I haven't mentioned any names, so now everybody's happy.
sentences.zh: 你看，我没提任何名字，所以现在大家都开心了。

sentences.en: I kind of feel like that character from Harry Potter,
sentences.zh: 我感觉自己就像《哈利·波特》里的那个角色，

sentences.en: Voldemort, who's the one who shall not be named, I guess.
sentences.zh: 伏地魔，那个“不可说名字的人”，我想是这样。

sentences.en: We called Senator Jeff Flake on Thursday.
sentences.zh: 我们周四致电了参议员杰夫·弗莱克。

sentences.en: Well, it's never something you want for the president of your own party to go after you, but it is what it is.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你绝不希望自己党派的总统来攻击你，但事实就是这样。

sentences.en: It's virtually unheard of for any sitting president to target a member of his own party like this.
sentences.zh: 在任总统像这样针对本党成员，几乎是闻所未闻的。

sentences.en: Jonathan Martin is a national political reporter.
sentences.zh: 乔纳森·马丁是一位全国政治记者。

sentences.en: This is so personally charged by what Flake has said about President Trump and his character, and so that's why Trump is lashing him back like he is.
sentences.zh: 这完全是因为弗莱克对特朗普总统及其人品的评价而引发的个人恩怨，这就是特朗普对他进行猛烈回击的原因。

sentences.en: He doesn't like Flake because Flake has criticized Trump.
sentences.zh: 他不喜欢弗莱克，因为弗莱克批评过他。

sentences.en: In terms of some of the policies that he has adopted and also, you know, his comportment or demeanor or manners.
sentences.zh: 就他所采取的一些政策，还有，你知道的，他的举止、风度或礼仪而言。

sentences.en: And I think being a conservative is not just adherence to conservative principles, and it also means that we ought to be, you know, decent.
sentences.zh: 我认为作为一名保守派，不仅仅是坚持保守派原则，还意味着我们应该，你知道的，体面一点。

sentences.en: You have to go back to the campaign for president when it was clear that Trump was coming on, and Senator Flake, who is in the Mormon church,
sentences.zh: 你得回溯到总统竞选时期，当时很明显特朗普正在崛起，而身为摩门教徒的弗莱克参议员，

sentences.en: and I think he had and has real character issues with Trump.
sentences.zh: 我认为他过去和现在都对特朗普有着真正的人品上的质疑。

sentences.en: Kind of on a moral basis.
sentences.zh: 某种程度上是基于道德层面。

sentences.en: Yes, but it really was elevated to a kind of thermonuclear political war when Senator Flake decided to write a book that he has titled Conscience of a Conservative,
sentences.zh: 是的，但当弗莱克参议员决定写一本名为《保守派的良心》的书时，这确实升级为一种热核政治战争，

sentences.en: basically about his critique of President Trump.
sentences.zh: 基本上是他对特朗普总统的批评。

sentences.en: It wasn't an easy decision to make.
sentences.zh: 这不是一个容易做出的决定。

sentences.en: It's easier not to.
sentences.zh: 不这么做更容易。

sentences.en: You know, the easiest path to re-election is to just go along and don't ruffle any feathers.
sentences.zh: 你知道，连任最简单的途径就是随大流，不要惹是生非。

sentences.en: And to follow the herd, if you will.
sentences.zh: 如果可以的话，就是随波逐流。

sentences.en: But I can tell you, I just, I don't think that I can do that.
sentences.zh: 但我可以告诉你，我只是，我不认为我能做到那样。

sentences.en: And I didn't tell my staff campaign or my official staff because, frankly, I didn't want to be talked out of it.
sentences.zh: 我没有告诉我的竞选团队或我的官方工作人员，因为坦白说，我不想被他们劝阻。

sentences.en: And they are good professionals, and they would have tried to talk me out of it, I think.
sentences.zh: 他们是专业的，我想他们肯定会试图劝我放弃。

sentences.en: And they should, because this is not the smartest political thing.
sentences.zh: 他们也确实应该劝我，因为从政治上讲，这并不是最明智的做法。

sentences.en: But I think it's important for the party.
sentences.zh: 但我认为这对党派很重要。

sentences.en: It's important for the conservative movement.
sentences.zh: 这对保守派运动很重要。

sentences.en: And I've been a Republican my entire life, and I care about where the party is.
sentences.zh: 我一生都是共和党人，我很关心我们党派的处境。

sentences.en: And I just don't think that we can be a governing majority much longer if we continue down this path.
sentences.zh: 如果继续沿着这条路走下去，我不认为我们还能维持多久的执政多数地位。

sentences.en: He has attacked the Republican Party for basically adopting what he calls a falcy and bargain when it comes to accepting President Trump and the party.
sentences.zh: 他抨击共和党基本上接受了他所说的“虚假交易”，即在接受特朗普总统和党派问题上的妥协。

sentences.en: And President Trump has lashed back.
sentences.zh: 而特朗普总统进行了猛烈回击。

sentences.en: He didn't miss an opportunity to attack him on Twitter on Wednesday morning.
sentences.zh: 周三早上，他没有错过在推特上攻击他的机会。

sentences.en: Phoenix crowd last night was amazing and a packed house, Trump tweeted.
sentences.zh: 特朗普发推说：“昨晚凤凰城的集会太棒了，座无虚席。”

sentences.en: I love the great state of Arizona.
sentences.zh: “我爱亚利桑那这个伟大的州。”

sentences.en: Not a fan of Jeff Flake.
sentences.zh: “我不喜欢杰夫·弗莱克。”

sentences.en: Weak on crime and border.
sentences.zh: “在犯罪和边境问题上软弱。”

sentences.en: The president goes after him where he thinks it hurts on policy grounds to talking about immigration a lot, which, of course, is front and center in Arizona, a border state.
sentences.zh: 总统在政策层面上攻击他认为对方痛处的地方，即大谈特谈移民问题，这当然是边境州亚利桑那的核心议题。

sentences.en: And Senator Flake is somebody who has been from the business wing of the party who is much more of a dove on immigration.
sentences.zh: 弗莱克参议员来自党内的商业派，在移民问题上更倾向于温和派。

sentences.en: And so the president knows that he's hurting him there with the base when he hits him on immigration.
sentences.zh: 所以总统知道，当他在移民问题上打击他时，是在动摇他的选民基础。

sentences.en: And when you say dove on immigration, what exactly does that mean in the case of Flake?
sentences.zh: 当你提到移民问题上的“温和派”时，在弗莱克的案例中具体指什么？

sentences.en: It means that he would support a comprehensive immigration overhaul that would include a pathway to legal status for legal immigrants.
sentences.zh: 这意味着他会支持全面的移民改革，包括为合法移民提供获得合法身份的途径。

sentences.en: So why is this conflict between them coming to a head right now?
sentences.zh: 那么为什么他们之间的冲突现在变得如此尖锐？

sentences.en: We are coming up against the period in which next year's budget will have to be agreed upon.
sentences.zh: 我们即将进入必须就明年预算达成一致的时期。

sentences.en: And will that include spending for the border wall that President Trump so fervently wants?
sentences.zh: 这是否会包括特朗普总统热切渴望的边境墙的支出？

sentences.en: And we are building a wall on the southern border, which is absolutely necessary.
sentences.zh: 我们正在南部边境修建一堵墙，这是绝对必要的。

sentences.en: Senator Flake, among others, is uneasy about that.
sentences.zh: 弗莱克参议员和其他人一样，对此感到不安。

sentences.en: But believe me, if we have to close down our government, we're building that wall.
sentences.zh: 但相信我，如果必须关闭政府，我们也会把那堵墙建起来。

sentences.en: Secondly, Senator Flake is coming up on his re-election next year, and the Republican Party is actively looking for primary challengers to take him out in the primary next year.
sentences.zh: 其次，弗莱克参议员明年面临连任，共和党正在积极寻找初选挑战者，试图在明年的初选中将他拉下马。

sentences.en: And that, by the way, includes President Trump, who met with some potential primary challengers to Flake when he was in Arizona backstage.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，这其中也包括特朗普总统，他在亚利桑那州期间曾在后台会见了一些弗莱克的潜在初选挑战者。

sentences.en: That's aggressive.
sentences.zh: 这太激进了。

sentences.en: That's very aggressive.
sentences.zh: 这非常激进。

sentences.en: You just don't see that kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 你根本看不到这种事情。

sentences.en: A president openly plotting with would-be challengers to a sitting senator.
sentences.zh: 一位总统公开与在任参议员的潜在挑战者密谋。

sentences.en: He has no institutional fidelity to the Republican Party.
sentences.zh: 他对共和党没有任何体制上的忠诚。

sentences.en: He is a lone operator.
sentences.zh: 他是一个独行侠。

sentences.en: He is somebody who borrowed the R after his name to get the nomination and win the presidency, but doesn't really give a damn about the Jeff Flakes of the world
sentences.zh: 他只是借用了共和党的名义来获得提名并赢得总统职位，但他根本不在乎像杰夫·弗莱克这样的人，

sentences.en: or the Mitch McConnells of the world.
sentences.zh: 或者像米奇·麦康奈尔这样的人。

sentences.en: He's about Donald J.
sentences.zh: 他只在乎唐纳德·J·

sentences.en: Trump.
sentences.zh: 特朗普。

sentences.en: And if you attack him, he's going to attack back.
sentences.zh: 如果你攻击他，他就会反击。

sentences.en: So you mentioned Mitch McConnell, the Senate Majority Leader.
sentences.zh: 你提到了参议院多数党领袖米奇·麦康奈尔。

sentences.en: What we're talking about is a larger tension, and you've been reporting on it, that's developed between the president and the entire Republican leadership in Congress.
sentences.zh: 我们谈论的是一个更大的紧张局势，你一直在报道它，即总统与国会整个共和党领导层之间已经形成的矛盾。

sentences.en: Help us understand that larger battle.
sentences.zh: 帮我们理解这场更大的斗争。

sentences.en: They are culturally very different people.
sentences.zh: 他们在文化上是非常不同的人。

sentences.en: I've been pretty candid with him and with all of you that I'm not a great fan of daily tweets.
sentences.zh: 我曾对他和你们所有人坦言，我不太喜欢每天发推特。

sentences.en: McConnell is cruel, deliberate, consumed with tactical victories and someone who does not say anything if he doesn't think it's going to work to achieve his goals.
sentences.zh: 麦康奈尔冷酷、审慎，沉迷于战术胜利，如果他认为某事无助于实现目标，他就什么都不会说。

sentences.en: And as we know, Trump is just the opposite of that.
sentences.zh: 正如我们所知，特朗普恰恰相反。

sentences.en: And so that clash has come to a head because the Senate could not repeal the Affordable Care Act.
sentences.zh: 这种冲突之所以激化，是因为参议院未能废除《平价医疗法案》。

sentences.en: The president took out his anger over that on Senator McConnell.
sentences.zh: 总统将对此的愤怒发泄在了麦康奈尔参议员身上。

sentences.en: But I said, Mitch, get to work and let's get it done.
sentences.zh: 但我说，米奇，开始工作吧，让我们把它完成。

sentences.en: They should have had this last one done.
sentences.zh: 他们本应该完成上一次投票的。

sentences.en: They lost by one vote.
sentences.zh: 他们以一票之差输了。

sentences.en: For a thing like that to happen is a disgrace.
sentences.zh: 发生这样的事情是一种耻辱。

sentences.en: You reported, Jonathan, along with Alex Burns, on a pretty extraordinary phone call between these two guys earlier this month.
sentences.zh: 乔纳森，你和亚历克斯·伯恩斯报道了本月初这两个人之间一次非常不寻常的通话。

sentences.en: What happened on that call?
sentences.zh: 那次通话发生了什么？

sentences.en: August 9th, the president at his golf club in Bedminster, New Jersey, called Senator McConnell in a fury.
sentences.zh: 8月9日，总统在新泽西州贝德明斯特的高尔夫俱乐部愤怒地致电麦康奈尔参议员。

sentences.en: And Senator McConnell had a local event in Kentucky that same week.
sentences.zh: 同一周，麦康奈尔参议员在肯塔基州有一个当地活动。

sentences.en: And part of the reason I think that the storyline is that we haven't done much is because, in part, the president and others have set these early timelines
sentences.zh: 我认为我们没做成什么事的原因之一，部分是因为总统和其他人设定了这些早期的时间表，

sentences.en: about things need to be done by a certain point.
sentences.zh: 关于事情需要在某个时间点完成。

sentences.en: Where he said something to the effect that the president and Trump didn't really understand the process, didn't quite get how Congress works.
sentences.zh: 他说了大意是总统和特朗普并不真正了解流程，不太明白国会是如何运作的。

sentences.en: Or democracy.
sentences.zh: 或者说不了解民主。

sentences.en: I remember, it was kind of diggy.
sentences.zh: 我记得，那话带点讽刺意味。

sentences.en: It was.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: Now, our new president had, of course, not been in this line of work before.
sentences.zh: 当然，我们的新总统以前没干过这一行。

sentences.en: And I think had excessive expectations about how quickly things happen in the democratic process.
sentences.zh: 我认为他对民主进程中事情发生的快慢有着过高的期望。

sentences.en: I think the combination of those two things, the failure of the bill and McConnell's critique, set him off.
sentences.zh: 我认为这两件事的结合，法案的失败和麦康奈尔的批评，让他彻底爆发了。

sentences.en: What was so striking about our reporting, though, is that that was what triggered the phone call.
sentences.zh: 不过，我们的报道最引人注目的是，那才是引发那次通话的原因。

sentences.en: But once he got on the phone with McConnell, he turned his attention to his other fixation, which is the Russia investigation.
sentences.zh: 但一旦他与麦康奈尔通上电话，他就把注意力转向了他另一个执念，即俄罗斯调查。

sentences.en: In the Senate.
sentences.zh: 在参议院的调查。

sentences.en: And the topic of Russia generally.
sentences.zh: 以及关于俄罗斯的总体话题。

sentences.en: And the suggestion being that Senator McConnell isn't doing enough to protect President Trump from that investigation.
sentences.zh: 暗示麦康奈尔参议员在保护特朗普总统免受调查方面做得不够。

sentences.en: So how heated did the conversation during this phone call become?
sentences.zh: 那么这次通话中的谈话变得有多激烈？

sentences.en: Raised voices, profanity, heated, and ugly were the two words that I got to describe it.
sentences.zh: 我得到的描述是：大声喧哗、脏话连篇、言辞激烈且丑陋。

sentences.en: Senator McConnell was elected in 1984 to the Senate.
sentences.zh: 麦康奈尔参议员于1984年当选参议员。

sentences.en: He was in legal office before that.
sentences.zh: 在此之前他担任过法律职务。

sentences.en: I don't think he's ever had a conversation with somebody who either was lateral to him or, you know, in a higher stature that was this demeaning.
sentences.zh: 我不认为他曾经与地位相当或更高的人进行过如此贬低人的谈话。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Why is McConnell engaging this?
sentences.zh: 为什么麦康奈尔要卷入其中？

sentences.en: Because from everything you're telling me about him, it's constitutionally not in his nature to be involved in this kind of a feud.
sentences.zh: 因为根据你告诉我关于他的一切，从性格上讲，他天生就不喜欢卷入这种争斗。

sentences.en: And it doesn't feel as out of character for Trump, but it feels out of character for McConnell and maybe even dangerous for him to be at odds with the president.
sentences.zh: 这对于特朗普来说并不反常，但对于麦康奈尔来说却显得反常，甚至与总统不和对他来说可能很危险。

sentences.en: Two issues here.
sentences.zh: 这里有两个问题。

sentences.en: Number one, McConnell's fixation is retaining his majority.
sentences.zh: 第一，麦康奈尔的执念是保住他的多数席位。

sentences.en: He's got a two-seat majority going into next year's midterm elections.
sentences.zh: 他在明年的中期选举中拥有两个席位的多数优势。

sentences.en: What he sees the president doing when the president attacks Jeff Flick is imperiling his,
sentences.zh: 他看到总统在攻击杰夫·弗莱克时，是在危及他，

sentences.en: Senator McConnell's, majority.
sentences.zh: 也就是麦康奈尔参议员的多数地位。

sentences.en: That hits close to home for him.
sentences.zh: 这让他感到了切肤之痛。

sentences.en: And ability to govern, right.
sentences.zh: 以及执政能力，对吧。

sentences.en: The second issue is President Trump repeatedly lecturing Senator McConnell about the rules of the Senate.
sentences.zh: 第二个问题是特朗普总统反复就参议院规则向麦康奈尔参议员说教。

sentences.en: It's a tweet from this morning, President Trump saying Republican Senate must get rid of 60 vote now.
sentences.zh: 这是今天早上的一条推文，特朗普总统说共和党参议院必须立即废除60票门槛。

sentences.en: It is killing the Republican Party, allows eight Democrats to control country.
sentences.zh: 这正在扼杀共和党，允许八名民主党人控制国家。

sentences.en: 200 bills sit in Senate.
sentences.zh: 200项法案堆在参议院。

sentences.en: A joke.
sentences.zh: 简直是个笑话。

sentences.en: That drives McConnell a little bit nutty as well because there aren't the votes to make that change.
sentences.zh: 这也让麦康奈尔有点抓狂，因为根本没有足够的票数来做出那种改变。

sentences.en: And President Trump routinely, like once every two weeks or so, hops on Twitter and says, change the rules of the Senate.
sentences.zh: 特朗普总统经常，大约每两周一次，跳上推特说，改变参议院规则。

sentences.en: The president says it's time to change Senate rules, simple majority rules.
sentences.zh: 总统说现在是改变参议院规则的时候了，实行简单多数规则。

sentences.en: You're the leader of the Senate.
sentences.zh: 你是参议院领袖。

sentences.en: Is it time to change rules?
sentences.zh: 是时候改变规则了吗？

sentences.en: No, it isn't.
sentences.zh: 不，不是。

sentences.en: There is an overwhelming majority on a bipartisan basis.
sentences.zh: 在两党基础上，绝大多数人（都反对）。

sentences.en: I'm not interested in changing the way the Senate operates on the legislative calendar.
sentences.zh: 我对改变参议院在立法日程上的运作方式不感兴趣。

sentences.en: And that will not happen.
sentences.zh: 那不会发生。

sentences.en: Why not?
sentences.zh: 为什么不？

sentences.en: It would fundamentally change the way the Senate has worked for a very long time.
sentences.zh: 那将从根本上改变参议院长期以来的运作方式。

sentences.en: We're not going to do that.
sentences.zh: 我们不会那样做。

sentences.en: Privately, he's saying even worse.
sentences.zh: 私下里，他说得更难听。

sentences.en: I think privately, he's bewildered that Trump has not adapted to the presidency.
sentences.zh: 我认为私下里，他对特朗普没有适应总统职位感到困惑。

sentences.en: He's bewildered that Trump doesn't understand that he is locked.
sentences.zh: 他困惑于特朗普不明白他已经被锁定了。

sentences.en: His fate is connected to the congressional Republicans, that he is not a separate player, that they are in this boat together.
sentences.zh: 他的命运与国会共和党人紧密相连，他不是一个独立的参与者，他们是在同一条船上。

sentences.en: And that if the congressional Republicans lose their majority in 2018, it's him, President Trump, whose neck is going to be on the line.
sentences.zh: 如果国会共和党人在2018年失去多数席位，那么面临危机的就是他，特朗普总统本人。

sentences.en: It leaves McConnell mystified.
sentences.zh: 这让麦康奈尔感到困惑。

sentences.en: Jonathan, how can it help the president's legislative agenda to be going after Republican leadership like McConnell?
sentences.zh: 乔纳森，攻击像麦康奈尔这样的共和党领导层，怎么可能有助于总统的立法议程？

sentences.en: It would seem to make it much harder to get anything done, which is already the source of his original frustration.
sentences.zh: 这似乎会让事情变得更难完成，而这本身就是他最初挫败感的来源。

sentences.en: That's exactly right.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: Why in the heck would he go after the leadership of his own party?
sentences.zh: 他到底为什么要攻击自己党派的领导层？

sentences.en: It makes no political sense, and it drives the Republican establishment and really all of
sentences.zh: 这在政治上毫无意义，它让共和党建制派，实际上让整个

sentences.en: Washington and sort of bonkers because it does not comport with anything in terms of how legislative victories are won.
sentences.zh: 华盛顿都感到抓狂，因为它与立法胜利的取得方式完全不符。

sentences.en: But he doesn't think that way.
sentences.zh: 但他并不这么想。

sentences.en: What he responds on Twitter, attacking Mitch McConnell, Lindsey Graham, Jeff, like, I don't
sentences.zh: 他在推特上的回应，攻击米奇·麦康奈尔、林赛·格雷厄姆、杰夫，就像，我不

sentences.en: think the thought of, well, what does this mean for the FY18 budget or lifting the debt ceiling or even tax reform?
sentences.zh: 认为他会去想，好吧，这对2018财年预算、提高债务上限甚至税改意味着什么？

sentences.en: What are the implications if I hit send on this?
sentences.zh: 如果我按下发送键，会有什么后果？

sentences.en: Is that going to hurt my cause a month from now?
sentences.zh: 这一个月后会损害我的事业吗？

sentences.en: That's just not how he operates.
sentences.zh: 他做事的方式根本不是这样的。

sentences.en: So I want to play devil's advocate for just a second.
sentences.zh: 所以我想从反面论证一下。

sentences.en: Can you outline a way in which the president's assault on Republicans in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 你能概括一下总统对美国共和党人的攻击，

sentences.en: Senate could theoretically be an effective strategy for him?
sentences.zh: 在理论上对他来说可能是一种有效的策略吗？

sentences.en: Is there any way to look at it that way?
sentences.zh: 有任何角度可以这样看吗？

sentences.en: You could.
sentences.zh: 你可以这样看。

sentences.en: That he would so whip up his loyalist in a lot of red states especially that they would come
sentences.zh: 他可能会在许多红州极大地煽动他的忠实支持者，以至于他们会

sentences.en: together and pressure Senate Republicans to toe the Trump line and to get behind whatever the president wants them to do.
sentences.zh: 团结起来，向参议院共和党人施压，要求他们遵循特朗普的路线，支持总统想要他们做的任何事情。

sentences.en: I mean, it's worth noting he said what he said about Jeff Flake in Jeff Flake's state.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，值得注意的是，他是在杰夫·弗莱克的州说了关于杰夫·弗莱克的那番话。

sentences.en: I mean, he's literally telling Jeff Flake's constituents, this guy is bad.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他实际上是在告诉杰夫·弗莱克的选民，这家伙很糟糕。

sentences.en: Vote him out.
sentences.zh: 把他投下去。

sentences.en: And he's more popular among the core base of the party in Arizona than Jeff Flake is.
sentences.zh: 而且他在亚利桑那州党内核心基础中的受欢迎程度比杰夫·弗莱克还要高。

sentences.en: Make no mistake about that.
sentences.zh: 对此不要有任何误解。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So that could work.
sentences.zh: 所以这可能会奏效。

sentences.en: Well, with Flake, I think it'll be interesting to see how he operates on the wall and if he
sentences.zh: 嗯，对于弗莱克，我认为看看他在边境墙问题上的表现会很有趣，如果他

sentences.en: feels pressure to fall in line on that vote now that Trump has pressured him, I think that will be revealing.
sentences.zh: 在特朗普施压后感到有压力要在投票中保持一致，我认为这将很有启发性。

sentences.en: And so that's where this really began is targeting McConnell and some other senators like Flake.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是这一切真正开始的地方，即针对麦康奈尔和其他像弗莱克这样的参议员。

sentences.en: And then with Charlottesville, what happened is Charlottesville gave the Republican senators
sentences.zh: 然后是夏洛茨维尔事件，夏洛茨维尔发生的事情给了共和党参议员们

sentences.en: a permission structure to really openly go after the president in a way that they really hadn't before.
sentences.zh: 一种许可机制，让他们能够真正公开地攻击总统，这是他们以前从未做过的。

sentences.en: What do you mean by permission?
sentences.zh: 你所说的许可机制是什么意思？

sentences.en: It suddenly allows them to make public.
sentences.zh: 它突然允许他们公开表达。

sentences.en: I say they, I mean the Senate Republicans were already crotchety because Trump was going after McConnell, going after Flake and a really sort of a frontal assault.
sentences.zh: 我说他们，是指参议院共和党人本来就已经很恼火了，因为特朗普在攻击麦康奈尔，攻击弗莱克，这简直是一种正面攻击。

sentences.en: And then the president responds to Charlottesville the way he did.
sentences.zh: 然后总统对夏洛茨维尔事件做出了那样的回应。

sentences.en: And all of a sudden they're horrified.
sentences.zh: 突然之间，他们感到震惊。

sentences.en: For them, that is political poison.
sentences.zh: 对他们来说，那是政治毒药。

sentences.en: They don't want to be associated with that.
sentences.zh: 他们不想与那种事情扯上关系。

sentences.en: And so I think that coming on the heels of the president attacking their colleagues, these guys had enough.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，在总统攻击他们的同事之后，这些人已经受够了。

sentences.en: And they said, you know, I'm not going to walk on eggshells anymore.
sentences.zh: 他们说，你知道，我不想再如履薄冰了。

sentences.en: I'm going to see what I think about this president.
sentences.zh: 我要看看我对这位总统有什么看法。

sentences.en: The president has not yet, has not yet been able to demonstrate the stability nor some of the competence that he needs to demonstrate in order to be successful.
sentences.zh: 总统尚未，尚未能够展现出他为了成功所需要的稳定性或某些能力。

sentences.en: So you're alluding to this, but to bring it full circle, we're now seeing McConnell defend
sentences.zh: 所以你提到了这一点，但为了总结一下，我们现在看到麦康奈尔在为

sentences.en: Jeff Flake against Trump's attacks.
sentences.zh: 杰夫·弗莱克辩护，抵御特朗普的攻击。

sentences.en: Is this going to be an increasing phenomenon, do you think, of Congress rallying together against the president?
sentences.zh: 你认为这会成为一种日益增长的现象吗，即国会团结起来反对总统？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I think when the president frontally attacks members of Congress, they are going to respond and they're going to stand up for each other.
sentences.zh: 我认为当总统正面攻击国会议员时，他们会做出回应，他们会互相支持。

sentences.en: So again, I would just advise a different style.
sentences.zh: 所以再次重申，我只是建议换一种风格。

sentences.en: You reach out to people.
sentences.zh: 你应该去接触人们。

sentences.en: You know, you're not shy about where you disagree.
sentences.zh: 你知道，对于你不同意的地方，不要羞于表达。

sentences.en: But again, don't make it personal.
sentences.zh: 但再次重申，不要针对个人。

sentences.en: And remember, these are members of your team and you've got a lot to get done this fall.
sentences.zh: 记住，这些人是你团队的成员，今年秋天你们有很多事情要完成。

sentences.en: You're going to need every vote you've got in the United States Senate.
sentences.zh: 你们在美国参议院需要每一张选票。

sentences.en: Jonathan, this is perhaps a hard question to answer, but do congressional Republicans want Donald Trump to be their president?
sentences.zh: 乔纳森，这可能是一个很难回答的问题，但国会共和党人希望唐纳德·特朗普成为他们的总统吗？

sentences.en: I think if you gave a lie detector test to certainly the Senate Republican caucus with the understanding that it would not be revealed who was saying what, I think the overwhelming
sentences.zh: 我想如果你对参议院共和党核心小组进行测谎，前提是不会透露是谁说了什么，我想绝大多数

sentences.en: majority of them would say that they don't think he should be president of the United States.
sentences.zh: 人会说他们认为他不应该成为美国总统。

sentences.en: And they would prefer Pence to be president, not tomorrow, but in an hour, maybe half an hour.
sentences.zh: 他们会更希望彭斯成为总统，不是明天，而是在一小时内，也许半小时内。

sentences.en: So speaking of this kind of candor you're talking about, Jeff Flake just a couple of days ago
sentences.zh: 说到你提到的这种坦率，杰夫·弗莱克就在几天前

sentences.en: said that President Trump should watch out for a primary challenge within his own party for the 2020 nomination.
sentences.zh: 说特朗普总统应该小心党内对他2020年提名的初选挑战。

sentences.en: Do you think the president's going to get a primary opponent in 2020, the way things are headed right now?
sentences.zh: 你认为总统在2020年会遇到初选对手吗，照目前的情况来看？

sentences.en: And then we'll let you go.
sentences.zh: 然后我们就让你离开。

sentences.en: You know, I don't know.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我不知道。

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: I think that certainly depends on him.
sentences.zh: 我认为这当然取决于他自己。

sentences.en: I think he could govern in a way that he wouldn't.
sentences.zh: 我认为他可以以一种不会遇到挑战的方式执政。

sentences.en: But I think that the way the direction he's headed right now, just kind of drilling down on the base rather than trying to expand the base, you know, I think he's inviting one.
sentences.zh: 但我认为他目前前进的方向，只是在巩固基本盘，而不是试图扩大基本盘，你知道，我认为他在招致挑战。

sentences.en: Which is a very unusual thing to say to your president.
sentences.zh: 这对你的总统来说是非常不同寻常的话。

sentences.en: Is what we're looking at a kind of snowballing towards Republicans in Congress trying to run a candidate against their own president?
sentences.zh: 我们看到的是国会共和党人试图推举一名候选人来对抗他们自己的总统，这是否正在像滚雪球一样发展？

sentences.en: There's no question that privately the congressional wing of the GOP does not want him to be on the ballot in 2020.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问，私下里，共和党的国会派系不希望他在2020年出现在选票上。

sentences.en: But a lot of them are constrained by the nature of their districts or their states from saying that publicly.
sentences.zh: 但他们中的许多人受到所在选区或州性质的限制，无法公开说出来。

sentences.en: How long does that restraint last?
sentences.zh: 这种克制能持续多久？

sentences.en: And what does the president do or say that may move more folks in the party to the Jeff
sentences.zh: 总统做了什么或说了什么，可能会促使党内更多人转向杰夫·弗莱克

sentences.en: Flake camp?
sentences.zh: 阵营？

sentences.en: Jonathan, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 乔纳森，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: Thanks, Mikey.
sentences.zh: 谢谢，麦基。

sentences.en: Senator Jeff Flake spoke with my colleague, Carl Hulse.
sentences.zh: 参议员杰夫·弗莱克与我的同事卡尔·赫尔斯进行了交谈。

sentences.en: Their full interview will be available tomorrow on our other podcast, The New Washington.
sentences.zh: 他们的完整采访将于明天在我们的另一个播客《新华盛顿》中播出。

sentences.en: It's good to be back.
sentences.zh: 很高兴回来。

sentences.en: You guys don't seem nearly as excited.
sentences.zh: 你们看起来一点也不兴奋。

sentences.en: I thought for sure there'd be balloons or...
sentences.zh: 我本以为肯定会有气球或者……

sentences.en: On Thursday afternoon, White House Press Secretary Sarah Huckabee Sanders was asked about the tense relationships between the president and congressional Republicans.
sentences.zh: 周四下午，白宫新闻秘书萨拉·赫卡比·桑德斯被问及总统与国会共和党人之间的紧张关系。

sentences.en: Look, I think the relationships are fine.
sentences.zh: 看，我认为关系很好。

sentences.en: Certainly there are going to be some policy differences, but there are also a lot of shared goals, and that's what we're focused on.
sentences.zh: 当然会有一些政策分歧，但也有很多共同目标，这才是我们关注的重点。

sentences.en: We're disappointed that Obamacare, they failed to get it repealed and replaced.
sentences.zh: 我们对奥巴马医改感到失望，他们未能成功废除并取代它。

sentences.en: But at the same time, President Trump has worked with Leader McConnell to reach out to other members and to work on those shared goals, and we're going to continue to do that when
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，特朗普总统与麦康奈尔领袖合作，接触其他成员并致力于这些共同目标，当

sentences.en: the Senate comes back from recess.
sentences.zh: 参议院休会回来后，我们将继续这样做。

sentences.en: From Senator Bob Corker, I'm sure you've seen him over a week ago about the president saying that the president has not yet been able to demonstrate the stability nor some of
sentences.zh: 关于鲍勃·科克参议员，我相信你一周多前看过他关于总统的言论，说总统尚未能够展现出他

sentences.en: the competence that he needs to demonstrate in order to be successful.
sentences.zh: 为了成功所需要的稳定性或某些能力。

sentences.en: He also said that he's not sure that the president understands the character of this nation.
sentences.zh: 他还说他不确定总统是否了解这个国家的品格。

sentences.en: Do you have any response to that?
sentences.zh: 你对此有什么回应吗？

sentences.en: I'm a Republican senator.
sentences.zh: 我是一名共和党参议员。

sentences.en: I think that's a ridiculous and outrageous claim and doesn't dignify a response from this podium.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一个荒谬且令人愤慨的说法，不值得在这个讲台上做出回应。

sentences.en: Major.
sentences.zh: 梅杰。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我是安德鲁·罗斯-索金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at the New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我为《纽约时报》的每日通讯《DealBook》报道商业和政策。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将采访一些商业、政治和文化领域最有影响力的人物，包括J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine Lagarde, Zilran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、齐尔兰·蒙达尼等等，在纽约市的DealBook峰会上现场直播。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以观看其中一些毫无防备、未经剪辑的对话。

sentences.zh: 我们将于11月18日在NYTimes.com上直播精选采访，供任何人免费观看。

If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅者，你可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序来观看，并获得一个月的免费访问权限，阅读我们所有的报道。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望你能收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你不会想错过的。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要知道的其他事情。

sentences.en: Mr. President, it's an honor to stand alongside you on your Independence Day.
sentences.zh: 总统先生，能在您的独立日与您并肩站在一起是我的荣幸。

sentences.en: On a visit to Ukraine, as it celebrates 25 years of independence from the Soviet Union,
sentences.zh: 在访问乌克兰之际，正值乌克兰庆祝脱离苏联独立25周年，

sentences.en: Defense Secretary Jim Mattis suggested the U.S.
sentences.zh: 国防部长吉姆·马蒂斯表示，美国

sentences.en: was prepared to supply Ukraine with lethal weapons to defend itself against an attack from Russia.
sentences.zh: 准备向乌克兰提供防御性武器，以抵御俄罗斯的攻击。

sentences.en: We do not and we will not accept Russia's seizure of the Crimea.
sentences.zh: 我们不接受，也不会接受俄罗斯对克里米亚的占领。

sentences.en: And despite Russia's denials, we know they are seeking to redraw international borders by force.
sentences.zh: 尽管俄罗斯否认，但我们知道他们正试图通过武力重绘国际边界。

sentences.en: The Obama administration had opposed sending so-called defensive weapons to Ukraine, fearing it would provoke Russia.
sentences.zh: 奥巴马政府曾反对向乌克兰输送所谓的防御性武器，担心这会激怒俄罗斯。

sentences.en: During a news conference on Thursday, Mattis was asked if the Trump administration felt differently.
sentences.zh: 在周四的新闻发布会上，马蒂斯被问及特朗普政府是否有不同的看法。

sentences.en: Defensive weapons are not provocative unless you're an aggressor.
sentences.zh: 防御性武器不是挑衅性的，除非你是侵略者。

sentences.en: And clearly, Ukraine is not an aggressor, such it's their own territory where the fighting is happening.
sentences.zh: 显然，乌克兰不是侵略者，战斗发生的地方是他们自己的领土。

sentences.en: Ukraine's president, Petro Poroshenko, agreed.
sentences.zh: 乌克兰总统彼得罗·波罗申科表示赞同。

sentences.en: Any defensive weapons, it would be just to increase the price if Russia make a decision to attack my troops and my territory.
sentences.zh: 任何防御性武器，都只是为了增加俄罗斯决定攻击我的军队和领土的代价。

sentences.en: And that would be strong motivation to stop them from the very irresponsible step.
sentences.zh: 这将是阻止他们采取这种非常不负责任的步骤的强大动力。

sentences.en: Pedro, thank you for 22 years of advocating for audio here at The New York Times.
sentences.zh: 佩德罗，感谢你为《纽约时报》的音频节目倡导了22年。

sentences.zh: 有关该节目的更多信息，包括我们采访的记者文章链接，请访问nytimes.com/thedaily。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这就是《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: See you Monday.
sentences.zh: 周一见。

sentences.zh: 本周在《Wirecutter秀》中，我们正在为假期接待客人做准备。

sentences.en: Tune in for tips on making your guests feel at home.
sentences.zh: 收听节目，获取让客人感到宾至如归的建议。

sentences.en: Are they a blackout sleeper?
sentences.zh: 他们是需要完全黑暗才能入睡的人吗？

sentences.en: I don't mean do they blackout to go to sleep.
sentences.zh: 我不是指他们是否会昏睡过去。

sentences.en: I mean, what kind of light do they require?
sentences.zh: 我是指，他们需要什么样的光线？

sentences.en: Because that is a very specific thing.
sentences.zh: 因为那是非常具体的事情。

sentences.en: Do they have allergies, food sensitivities?
sentences.zh: 他们有过敏症或食物敏感吗？

sentences.en: Are they coffee tea drinkers?
sentences.zh: 他们是喝咖啡还是喝茶的人？

sentences.en: What time do they like to get up?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢几点起床？

sentences.en: Find The Wirecutter Show on The New York Times app or wherever you like to listen.
sentences.zh: 在《纽约时报》应用程序上或你喜欢的任何地方收听《Wirecutter秀》。
